title: Part II: Issue and Redemption of Debentures

topics.title: Debentures: meaning and comparison with shares

learn.hook: When NHAI or a big company raises money through bonds, investors become lenders, not owners. That loan certificate is a debenture.
points: A debenture is a written acknowledgement of a debt by a company under its common seal (where used), carrying a fixed rate of interest and repayable as per terms.
A debenture trust deed appoints trustees to protect debenture-holders' interests and records terms like interest, security and redemption.
Debentures and bonds are borrowed (debt) capital; debenture-holders are creditors of the company.

Shares vs debentures: shareholders are owners, get dividend (an appropriation, paid only from profits) and have voting rights; debenture-holders are creditors, get interest (a charge, payable even in a loss), have no voting rights, may be secured, and are repaid before shareholders on winding up.
Debentures may be issued at a discount; shares cannot (except sweat equity). Debentures may be convertible into shares.

example.q: Neha buys 50 9% debentures of ₹100 each. The company makes a loss this year. Does she get interest? How much?
steps: Interest on debentures is a charge, payable whether there is profit or loss.

learn.reallife: Indian Railways' financing arm IRFC and many PSUs raise thousands of crores through bonds that work just like debentures.

games.title: Share or debenture?
items: Repaid before owners on winding up

games.title: Debenture facts
items: Debenture interest is payable even if the company makes a loss.
It is a charge on profits.
Debenture-holders have voting rights in the general meeting.
They are creditors and do not vote.
A debenture is an acknowledgement of debt.
It certifies a loan to the company.
Debentures cannot be issued at a discount.
Unlike shares, debentures can be issued at a discount.
A debenture trust deed protects debenture-holders' interests.

quiz.q: A debenture is:
options: an acknowledgement of debt by a company carrying a fixed rate of interest
a unit of ownership in a company
quiz.explain: It certifies that the company has borrowed money.
steps: A debenture is a written acknowledgement of debt by a company.
It carries a fixed rate of interest and is repayable as per terms.
Answer: an acknowledgement of debt by a company carrying a fixed rate of interest

quiz.q: Debenture-holders are:
quiz.explain: They lend money; they do not own the company.
steps: Debenture-holders lend money to the company.
So they are its creditors, not owners.
Answer: creditors of the company

quiz.q: Which is TRUE of debentures but NOT of shares?
options: The return is paid only out of profits
The return is a fixed interest payable even if there is a loss
They cannot be issued at a discount
quiz.explain: Debenture interest is a charge; dividend is an appropriation of profit.
steps: Debenture interest is a charge, fixed and payable even in a loss.
Voting rights and returns only from profit belong to shares; shares cannot be issued at a discount.
Answer: The return is a fixed interest payable even if there is a loss
quiz.mistake: Gives debentures the features of shares

quiz.q: Interest on 50 9% debentures of ₹100 each for a year:
steps: Answer: ₹450

quiz.q: On winding up, debenture-holders are repaid:
options: only if there is a surplus after shareholders
quiz.explain: As creditors, they rank ahead of owners.
steps: Debenture-holders are creditors.
Creditors rank ahead of owners, so they are repaid before shareholders.
Answer: before shareholders

quiz.q: The document that records the terms of a debenture issue and appoints trustees is the:
quiz.explain: The trust deed protects debenture-holders through trustees.
steps: The debenture trust deed appoints trustees and records interest, security and redemption terms.
Answer: debenture trust deed

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): Debenture-holders do not have voting rights.
Reason (R): Debenture-holders are creditors and not owners of the company.
options: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
A is false, but R is true
quiz.explain: Voting is an ownership right; creditors do not get it.
steps: A: debenture-holders have no voting rights – true.
R: they are creditors, not owners – true.
Voting is an ownership right, so R explains A.
Answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.mistake: Does not connect voting to ownership

quiz.q: Bonds and debentures together are best described as:
quiz.explain: They represent money lent to the company.
steps: Bonds and debentures represent money lent to the company.
So they are borrowed (debt) capital.
Answer: borrowed (debt) capital

teach.ask: Gappu wants to invest but can't decide between shares and debentures. Explain the difference.
teach.praise: Perfect! Debenture-holders are creditors earning interest; shareholders are owners earning dividend with votes.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: does a debenture-holder get interest when the company makes a loss?

revise.summary: A debenture is a written acknowledgement of debt with a fixed rate of interest. Debenture-holders are creditors: they get interest (a charge) even in a loss, have no voting rights, may be secured and are repaid before shareholders.
focus: Meaning of debenture and debenture trust deed
remember: Debenture-holders are creditors
Interest: a charge, payable even in a loss
Dividend: an appropriation, only from profits
Debentures can be issued at a discount; shares cannot (except sweat equity)
traps: Debenture-holders are not owners and cannot vote
Debenture interest is not paid only out of profits
Debentures are borrowed, not owned, capital

learn.hook: Secured or naked, perpetual or redeemable, convertible or not, zero coupon or not, registered or bearer – debentures come in many flavours.
points: Security: secured debentures carry a charge on assets; unsecured (naked) debentures have no such charge.
Tenure: redeemable debentures are repaid after a fixed period; perpetual (irredeemable) debentures are not repayable during the life of the company.
Convertibility: fully convertible (wholly into shares), partly convertible, and non-convertible debentures (NCDs).
Coupon rate: specific coupon rate debentures carry a stated interest rate; zero coupon rate debentures carry no interest but are issued at a deep discount and redeemed at face value.
Registration: registered debentures – holders' names recorded and transfer needs a transfer deed; bearer debentures – transferable by mere delivery, interest paid to whoever holds the coupon.

example.q: A company issues debentures of face value ₹1,000 at ₹750, with no interest, redeemable at ₹1,000 after 5 years. What type is it, and what does the investor earn?
steps: No interest → zero coupon rate debenture.
Investor's return = 1,000 − 750 = ₹250 at redemption.
example.answer: Zero coupon debenture; return ₹250 per debenture.

learn.reallife: Indian investors buy NCDs from NBFCs for steady interest, while many PSU bonds are secured and redeemable after a fixed tenure.

games.title: Type ↔ feature
pairs: Carries a charge on company assets
No interest; issued at a deep discount
Not repayable during the company's life

quiz.q: Debentures that carry a charge on the company's assets are:
quiz.explain: A charge on assets gives security to holders.
steps: A charge on the company's assets gives security.
Such debentures are secured debentures.
Answer: secured debentures

quiz.q: Unsecured debentures are also called:
quiz.explain: 'Naked' means without any security.
steps: Unsecured debentures have no charge on assets.
They are called naked debentures.
Answer: naked debentures

quiz.q: Debentures that are not repayable during the life of the company are:
quiz.explain: They are repaid only on winding up.
steps: Debentures not repayable during the company's life are perpetual (irredeemable).
They are repaid only on winding up.
Answer: perpetual (irredeemable) debentures

quiz.q: A zero coupon debenture of face value ₹1,000 is issued at ₹750 and redeemed at ₹1,000. The investor's return per debenture:
quiz.explain: No interest is paid; the gain is the difference between redemption and issue price.
steps: Zero coupon: no interest; gain = redemption price − issue price.
Answer: ₹250
quiz.mistake: Thinks zero coupon means zero return

quiz.q: Debentures transferable by mere delivery are:
quiz.explain: No transfer deed is needed for bearer debentures.
steps: Bearer debentures pass by mere delivery, with no transfer deed.
Answer: bearer debentures

quiz.q: Debentures that will be converted into equity shares only partly are:
quiz.explain: Only a portion converts; the rest is redeemed.
steps: Only a portion converts into equity; the rest is redeemed.
These are partly convertible debentures.
Answer: partly convertible debentures

quiz.q: NCDs commonly offered by NBFCs in India are:
quiz.explain: NCD = non-convertible debenture; they cannot become shares.
steps: NCD = non-convertible debenture, which cannot become shares.
Answer: non-convertible debentures

quiz.q: Registered debentures differ from bearer debentures because:
options: holders' names are recorded in the company's register and transfer needs a transfer deed
quiz.explain: Registration is about how ownership is recorded and transferred.
steps: Registered debentures record holders' names in the register.
Their transfer needs a transfer deed; bearer ones pass by delivery.
Answer: holders' names are recorded in the company's register and transfer needs a transfer deed
quiz.mistake: Links registration with interest or security

teach.ask: Gappu is browsing debentures. Explain the main types.
teach.praise: Fantastic! Security, tenure, convertibility, coupon and registration – Gappu can read any debenture label now.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: what is special about a zero coupon debenture?

revise.summary: Debentures are classified by security (secured, naked), tenure (redeemable, perpetual), convertibility (fully, partly, non-convertible), coupon rate (specific, zero coupon) and registration (registered, bearer).
focus: Each basis of classification and its types
Return on a zero coupon debenture
remember: Naked = unsecured
Perpetual = irredeemable during company's life
Zero coupon: no interest, issued at deep discount, redeemed at face value
Bearer: transfer by delivery
traps: Zero coupon debentures pay no interest; the gain is the discount
Naked debentures are unsecured, not convertible
Registered debentures need a transfer deed

topics.title: Issue of debentures for cash at par, premium or discount

learn.hook: Like shares, debentures can be issued in one go or in instalments – and unlike shares, they may be issued at a discount.
points: Lump sum / instalments: Bank Dr / Debenture Application & Allotment Cr; then Debenture Application & Allotment Dr / Debentures Cr. Calls are recorded like share calls.
At premium: Debenture Application & Allotment Dr (issue price) / Debentures Cr (face value), Securities Premium Cr (premium).
At discount: Debenture Application & Allotment Dr (issue price), Discount on Issue of Debentures Dr (discount) / Debentures Cr (face value).
Securities premium on debentures can be used as per Section 52, e.g. to write off discount or loss on issue of debentures.
Over-subscription: excess application money is refunded (Debenture Application & Allotment Dr / Bank Cr) or adjusted towards allotment.

example.q: A company issues 5,000 9% debentures of ₹100 each at a discount of 10%, payable fully on application. Pass the entries.
steps: Cash received = 5,000 × 90 = ₹4,50,000: Bank Dr / Debenture Application & Allotment Cr.
Debenture Application & Allotment Dr 4,50,000, Discount on Issue of Debentures Dr 50,000 / 9% Debentures Cr 5,00,000.

learn.reallife: Infrastructure companies in India often issue debentures at a premium when credit ratings are strong, and at a discount when markets are nervous.

items.text: At a premium, the extra over face value is credited to ___ Premium.
At a discount, ___ on Issue of Debentures is debited.
Debentures account is always credited with the ___ value.
Refund of excess application money: Dr Debenture Application & Allotment, Cr ___.

items.q: 2,000 debentures of ₹500 at par: debentures credited

quiz.q: 5,000 9% debentures of ₹100 issued at a 10% discount, fully payable on application. Amount credited to 9% Debentures A/c:
quiz.explain: Debentures are always credited at face value.
steps: Debentures are always credited at face value.

quiz.q: In the same case, Discount on Issue of Debentures:
steps: Discount = 10% of ₹100 = ₹10 per debenture.
Answer: ₹50,000
quiz.mistake: Calculates discount on number of debentures only

quiz.q: 5,000 debentures of ₹100 issued at ₹105. Securities premium:
quiz.explain: Premium ₹5 × 5,000.
steps: Premium per debenture = 105 − 100 = ₹5.
Answer: ₹25,000
quiz.mistake: Credits the full issue price to premium

quiz.q: Entry on allotment of debentures issued at a premium:
options: Debentures A/c Dr / Securities Premium A/c Cr
Bank A/c Dr / Debentures A/c Cr only
Securities Premium A/c Dr / Debentures A/c Cr
Debenture Application & Allotment A/c Dr / Debentures A/c Cr, Securities Premium A/c Cr
quiz.explain: The issue price is split into face value and premium.
steps: The issue price is split into face value and premium.
Entry: Debenture Application & Allotment A/c Dr, Debentures A/c Cr, Securities Premium A/c Cr.
Answer: Debenture Application & Allotment A/c Dr / Debentures A/c Cr, Securities Premium A/c Cr

quiz.q: A company offers 5,000 debentures of ₹100 at par, payable in full on application, and receives applications for 7,000. Excess applications are rejected. Refund:
steps: Excess applications = 7,000 − 5,000 = 2,000.

quiz.q: Which statement is correct about issue price?
options: Neither shares nor debentures can be issued at a discount
Debentures may be issued at a discount, but shares (except sweat equity) cannot
Both may be issued at any discount
Only shares may be issued at a discount
quiz.explain: Section 53 bars discount on shares, not debentures.
steps: Section 53 bars issuing shares at a discount (except sweat equity).
It does not bar debentures.
So debentures may be issued at a discount, but shares cannot.
Answer: Debentures may be issued at a discount, but shares (except sweat equity) cannot
quiz.mistake: Applies the share rule to debentures

quiz.q: Securities premium received on debentures can be used to:
options: write off discount or loss on issue of debentures
quiz.explain: Section 52 permits this use.
steps: Section 52 allows securities premium to write off discount or loss on issue of debentures.
It cannot pay interest, dividend or salaries.
Answer: write off discount or loss on issue of debentures

quiz.q: Debentures of ₹100 issued at 8% discount, payable ₹40 on application and the rest on allotment. Amount due on allotment per debenture:
quiz.explain: Issue price ₹92 less ₹40 on application.
steps: Issue price = 100 − 8% of 100 = 92
Due on allotment = 92 − 40 = 52
Answer: ₹52

teach.ask: Gappu's company issued debentures at a discount. Explain the entries for par, premium and discount.
teach.praise: Great! Debentures at face value, premium to Securities Premium, discount debited to a discount account.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: at what value is the Debentures account always credited?

revise.summary: Debentures issued for cash are credited at face value. A premium is credited to Securities Premium; a discount is debited to Discount on Issue of Debentures. Excess applications are refunded or adjusted.
focus: Entries for issue at par, premium and discount
remember: Debentures always credited at face value
Premium → Securities Premium Cr
Discount → Discount on Issue of Debentures Dr
traps: Don't credit debentures at issue price
Debentures can be issued at a discount; shares cannot
Securities premium cannot be used for dividends or interest

topics.title: Debentures issued for consideration other than cash

learn.hook: A company buys a business and pays with debentures. The seller becomes a lender to the company.
points: First record the purchase: Sundry Assets Dr (and Goodwill Dr if needed) / Sundry Liabilities Cr, Vendor Cr (purchase consideration), Capital Reserve Cr (if consideration < net assets).
Then issue debentures: Vendor Dr / Debentures Cr (face value), Securities Premium Cr (if at premium); for discount, Discount on Issue Dr.
Number of debentures = Purchase consideration ÷ Issue price.
Goodwill = Purchase consideration − Net assets (if positive). Capital reserve = Net assets − Purchase consideration (if positive).

example.q: Assets ₹5,50,000 and liabilities ₹50,000 are taken over for ₹4,80,000, paid by 10% debentures of ₹100 at a 20% premium. Find capital reserve and number of debentures.
steps: Issue price = ₹120; debentures = 4,80,000 ÷ 120 = 4,000.
Vendor Dr 4,80,000 / 10% Debentures Cr 4,00,000, Securities Premium Cr 80,000.

learn.reallife: Acquisitions in Indian manufacturing sometimes pay sellers in debentures, giving them steady interest while the buyer conserves cash.

games.title: Non-cash debenture issue
items: Number of debentures = purchase consideration ÷ face value, even at a premium.
If purchase consideration is more than net assets, goodwill is debited.
When debentures are issued to the vendor, the vendor's account is debited.
Capital reserve arises when the company pays more than net assets.
Capital reserve arises when it pays less.

quiz.q: Assets ₹5,50,000 and liabilities ₹50,000 are bought for ₹4,80,000. Capital reserve:
quiz.explain: Net assets ₹5,00,000 exceed the consideration by ₹20,000.
steps: Answer: ₹20,000

quiz.q: Purchase consideration ₹4,80,000 is paid by 10% debentures of ₹100 at a 20% premium. Number of debentures:
steps: Issue price = 100 + 20% = ₹120.
Answer: 4,000

quiz.q: In the same case, amount credited to Securities Premium on issuing the debentures:
steps: Premium per debenture = ₹20; debentures = 4,000.
Securities premium = 4,000 × 20 = ₹80,000.
Answer: ₹80,000

quiz.q: Purchase consideration ₹2,70,000 is paid by issuing ₹100 debentures at a 10% discount. Number of debentures:
steps: Issue price = 100 − 10% = ₹90.
Answer: 3,000

quiz.q: Net assets ₹5,00,000 are acquired for ₹5,40,000. The difference is:
quiz.explain: Paying more than net assets means goodwill is purchased.
steps: Consideration ₹5,40,000 > net assets ₹5,00,000.
Paying more means goodwill of ₹40,000 is debited.
Answer: goodwill, debited
quiz.mistake: Mixes up goodwill and capital reserve

quiz.q: Entry to issue debentures to a vendor at par:
options: Debentures A/c Dr / Vendor A/c Cr
Vendor A/c Dr / Debentures A/c Cr
Bank A/c Dr / Debentures A/c Cr
Vendor A/c Dr / Bank A/c Cr
quiz.explain: Issuing debentures discharges the amount owed to the vendor.
steps: Issuing debentures discharges the vendor's claim.
Entry: Vendor A/c Dr, Debentures A/c Cr.
Answer: Vendor A/c Dr / Debentures A/c Cr

quiz.q: Net assets ₹4,00,000 are acquired for ₹4,40,000, paid in 9% debentures of ₹100 at a 10% premium. Goodwill and number of debentures:
steps: Issue price = ₹110; debentures = 4,40,000 ÷ 110 = 4,000.
Answer: Goodwill ₹40,000; 4,000 debentures
quiz.mistake: Divides by face value or reverses goodwill and capital reserve

quiz.q: Purchase of a business: assets taken over are recorded as:
options: Vendor A/c Dr / Sundry Assets A/c Cr
Debentures A/c Dr / Sundry Assets A/c Cr
Sundry Assets A/c Dr / Debentures A/c Cr directly
Sundry Assets A/c Dr / Sundry Liabilities A/c Cr, Vendor A/c Cr
quiz.explain: Purchase is recorded first; payment through debentures follows.
steps: First record the purchase: assets in, liabilities and vendor out.
Entry: Sundry Assets A/c Dr, Sundry Liabilities A/c Cr, Vendor A/c Cr.
Answer: Sundry Assets A/c Dr / Sundry Liabilities A/c Cr, Vendor A/c Cr

teach.ask: Gappu's company bought a business and paid with debentures. Explain the steps.
teach.praise: Spot on! Record the purchase, then issue debentures to the vendor at the issue price.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: how is the number of debentures worked out?

revise.summary: When debentures are issued for assets or a business, the purchase is recorded first (Assets Dr / Liabilities and Vendor Cr, with goodwill or capital reserve), then the vendor is paid by issuing debentures at par, premium or discount.
focus: Entries for purchase and for issuing debentures to the vendor
Number of debentures = consideration ÷ issue price
remember: Number of debentures = purchase consideration ÷ issue price
Goodwill = consideration − net assets
Capital reserve = net assets − consideration
traps: Divide by the issue price, not the face value
Paying more than net assets gives goodwill, not capital reserve
Record the purchase before the debenture issue

learn.hook: A bank lends ₹10 lakh but wants extra comfort. The company hands over its own debentures as a backup pledge – collateral security.
points: Collateral security is a subsidiary or additional security given besides the primary security for a loan. The lender can sell the debentures only if the borrower defaults.
No interest is paid on debentures issued as collateral (interest is paid only on the actual loan).
First method: no journal entry; the fact is shown in a note under the loan in Long-term Borrowings.
Second method: Debenture Suspense A/c Dr / Debentures A/c Cr (face value). In the balance sheet, debentures are shown under Long-term Borrowings and Debenture Suspense is deducted from them.
When the loan is repaid, the debentures are cancelled (reverse entry under the second method).

example.q: A company takes a bank loan of ₹10,00,000 and issues 12,000 9% debentures of ₹100 each as collateral. Show the second method.
steps: Debenture Suspense A/c Dr 12,00,000 / 9% Debentures A/c Cr 12,00,000.
Balance sheet note: 9% Debentures 12,00,000 less Debenture Suspense 12,00,000 = nil; Bank Loan 10,00,000 (secured by collateral debentures).

learn.reallife: MSMEs borrowing from SBI often pledge extra security; companies can do the same with their own debentures.

items.text: Under the second method, ___ Suspense A/c is debited.
Under the first method, ___ journal entry is passed.
Collateral debentures are shown under Long-term ___.

games.title: Collateral checks
items: Collateral debentures carry interest like normal debentures.
Interest is paid only on the loan.
Under the first method, the issue is disclosed only in a note.
Under the second method, Debenture Suspense is deducted from debentures in the balance sheet.
So the net effect is nil.
The lender can sell collateral debentures even if the borrower repays on time.
Collateral security is additional to the primary security.

quiz.q: Debentures issued as collateral security means debentures:
options: given as additional security for a loan, enforceable only on default
sold to the public for cash
quiz.explain: They back a loan; the lender realises them only if the company defaults.
steps: Collateral debentures are additional security for a loan.
The lender can sell them only if the company defaults.
Answer: given as additional security for a loan, enforceable only on default

quiz.q: Interest on debentures issued as collateral security is:
quiz.explain: Interest is paid on the loan itself, not on the collateral debentures.
steps: Interest is paid on the actual loan.
So no interest is payable on collateral debentures.
Answer: not payable

quiz.q: Under the first method of recording collateral debentures:
options: no entry is made; a note is given under the loan
quiz.explain: The loan account carries a note about the collateral.
steps: First method: no journal entry.
A note under the loan shows the collateral.
Answer: no entry is made; a note is given under the loan

quiz.q: Under the second method, the entry for issuing ₹12,00,000 debentures as collateral is:
options: Debentures A/c Dr / Debenture Suspense A/c Cr ₹12,00,000
Bank A/c Dr / Debentures A/c Cr ₹12,00,000
Bank Loan A/c Dr / Debentures A/c Cr ₹12,00,000
Debenture Suspense A/c Dr / Debentures A/c Cr ₹12,00,000
quiz.explain: Suspense is debited and Debentures credited at face value.
steps: Second method: debit Debenture Suspense and credit Debentures at face value.
Entry: Debenture Suspense A/c Dr, Debentures A/c Cr ₹12,00,000.
Answer: Debenture Suspense A/c Dr / Debentures A/c Cr ₹12,00,000
quiz.mistake: Reverses the entry or records cash

quiz.q: 12,000 9% debentures of ₹100 are issued as collateral. Amount debited to Debenture Suspense:
quiz.explain: Face value 12,000 × 100.
steps: Debenture Suspense is debited at face value.

quiz.q: In the balance sheet (second method), Debenture Suspense is:
options: deducted from the debentures under Long-term Borrowings
quiz.explain: Deducting it shows that no real liability arises from collateral debentures.
steps: Debenture Suspense is deducted from the debentures under Long-term Borrowings.
This shows no real liability arises.
Answer: deducted from the debentures under Long-term Borrowings

quiz.q: When the loan secured by collateral debentures is repaid (second method), the entry is:
options: Debenture Suspense A/c Dr / Debentures A/c Cr
Debentures A/c Dr / Bank A/c Cr
Debentures A/c Dr / Debenture Suspense A/c Cr
quiz.explain: The collateral debentures are cancelled by reversing the original entry.
steps: When the loan is repaid, the collateral debentures are cancelled.
Reverse the entry: Debentures A/c Dr, Debenture Suspense A/c Cr.
Answer: Debentures A/c Dr / Debenture Suspense A/c Cr

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): Debentures issued as collateral are not a real liability of the company.
Reason (R): They become a claim only if the company fails to repay the loan.
options: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.explain: Their liability is contingent on default, so they are offset or noted.
steps: A: collateral debentures are not a real liability – true.
R: they become a claim only on default – true.
Being contingent on default is why they are not a real liability.
Answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.mistake: Fails to link the default condition

teach.ask: Gappu's bank wants extra security for a loan. Explain debentures as collateral and both methods.
teach.praise: Excellent! Collateral debentures are backup security – no interest, and two ways of showing them.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: does the company pay interest on debentures given as collateral?

revise.summary: Debentures may be issued as collateral (additional) security for a loan, carrying no interest. Either no entry is made with a note under the loan, or Debenture Suspense is debited and Debentures credited, with the suspense deducted in the balance sheet.
focus: Balance sheet presentation and cancellation on repayment
remember: No interest on collateral debentures
Second method: Debenture Suspense Dr / Debentures Cr (face value)
Debenture Suspense deducted from debentures under Long-term Borrowings
traps: Don't pay interest on collateral debentures
Don't show collateral debentures as an extra real liability
The first method needs no journal entry

topics.title: Terms of issue and redemption of debentures

learn.hook: Issue at par, premium or discount; redeem at par or at a premium – six combinations, one rule: put any loss in a 'loss on issue' account up front.
points: Six cases: issued at par/premium/discount × redeemable at par/premium.
If redeemable at a premium, record the premium payable on redemption as a liability (Premium on Redemption of Debentures A/c Cr) at the time of issue, and debit Loss on Issue of Debentures A/c.
Issue at discount, redeemable at premium: Loss on Issue = discount + premium on redemption.
Issue at premium, redeemable at premium: Securities Premium Cr (issue premium) and Premium on Redemption Cr; Loss on Issue Dr = redemption premium.
Actual redemption of debentures (methods, DRR, sinking fund) is outside the CBSE syllabus for this course.

example.q: 1,000 debentures of ₹100 are issued at a 5% discount and redeemable at a 10% premium. Pass the issue entry (cash received in full).
steps: Loss on Issue of Debentures Dr 15,000 (discount 5,000 + redemption premium 10,000).
Debentures Cr 1,00,000; Premium on Redemption of Debentures Cr 10,000.
example.answer: Bank ₹95,000 + Loss ₹15,000 = Debentures ₹1,00,000 + Premium on Redemption ₹10,000

learn.reallife: Corporate bonds sold to Indian mutual funds often promise a redemption premium – the company records that future cost as a liability right at issue.

games.title: Debit or credit in the issue entry?

quiz.q: 1,000 debentures of ₹100 issued at 5% discount, redeemable at 10% premium. Loss on Issue of Debentures:
quiz.explain: Discount ₹5,000 + premium on redemption ₹10,000.
steps: Discount = 5% of 100 = 5; redemption premium = 10% of 100 = 10
Loss per debenture = 5 + 10 = 15
Loss on issue = 1,000 × 15 = 15,000
Answer: ₹15,000

quiz.q: Debentures issued at par, redeemable at a 10% premium. The issue entry is:
options: Bank Dr, Loss on Issue Dr / Debentures Cr, Premium on Redemption Cr
Bank Dr / Debentures Cr, Securities Premium Cr
Bank Dr, Premium on Redemption Dr / Debentures Cr
quiz.explain: The redemption premium is a future liability recorded now, with a matching loss.
steps: Issued at par, so no issue premium or discount.
Redemption premium is a future liability recorded now with a matching loss.
Entry: Bank Dr, Loss on Issue Dr / Debentures Cr, Premium on Redemption Cr.
Answer: Bank Dr, Loss on Issue Dr / Debentures Cr, Premium on Redemption Cr

quiz.q: Premium on Redemption of Debentures account is:
quiz.explain: The company owes this extra amount to holders at redemption.
steps: The company owes the redemption premium to holders at redemption.
So it is a liability.
Answer: a liability, payable at redemption

quiz.q: 2,000 debentures of ₹100 issued at ₹105, redeemable at ₹110. Loss on issue:
quiz.explain: Loss on issue equals premium on redemption ₹10 × 2,000; the ₹5 issue premium goes to securities premium.
steps: Issue premium ₹5 goes to Securities Premium.
Loss on issue = redemption premium = 2,000 × ₹10 = ₹20,000.
Answer: ₹20,000
quiz.mistake: Nets off the issue premium against the loss

quiz.q: In the same case (₹105 issue, ₹110 redemption), securities premium credited:
quiz.explain: Issue premium ₹5 × 2,000.
steps: Issue premium = 105 − 100 = ₹5.
Securities premium = 2,000 × 5 = ₹10,000.
Answer: ₹10,000
quiz.mistake: Confuses issue premium with redemption premium

quiz.q: Debentures issued at a 5% discount, redeemable at par. Per ₹100 debenture, the amount debited to Discount on Issue:
quiz.explain: Only the issue discount arises.
steps: Issued at ₹95, redeemable at par.
Only the issue discount arises: 100 − 95 = ₹5 per debenture.
Answer: ₹5
quiz.mistake: Adds a redemption premium that does not exist

quiz.q: Which case gives NO loss or discount on issue?
options: Issued at par, redeemable at premium
Issued at discount, redeemable at par
Issued at par, redeemable at par
Issued at premium, redeemable at premium
quiz.explain: With par on both ends, no extra cost arises.
steps: Issued at par and redeemable at par: no premium, discount or loss arises.
Answer: Issued at par, redeemable at par
quiz.mistake: Thinks premium on issue offsets redemption premium

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT in the CBSE syllabus for this chapter?
options: Issue of debentures as collateral security
Creating a Debenture Redemption Reserve and sinking fund
quiz.explain: Actual redemption and DRR are excluded.
steps: Actual redemption, DRR and sinking fund are outside the syllabus.
So creating a DRR and sinking fund is NOT in it.
Answer: Creating a Debenture Redemption Reserve and sinking fund
quiz.mistake: Thinks all debenture topics are examined

teach.ask: Gappu's company issues debentures at a discount, redeemable at a premium. Explain the issue entry.
teach.praise: Brilliant! Debit loss on issue for discount plus redemption premium, and credit premium on redemption as a liability.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: why is the premium on redemption recorded at the time of issue?

revise.summary: Debentures may be issued at par, premium or discount and redeemed at par or premium. A redemption premium is recorded at issue as a liability with a matching Loss on Issue; discount plus redemption premium both form the loss.
focus: The six terms of issue and redemption
Entries at the time of issue
remember: Redemption premium: credit Premium on Redemption, debit Loss on Issue
Discount + redemption premium = loss on issue
Issue premium → Securities Premium
traps: Issue premium does not reduce the loss on issue
Premium on Redemption is a liability, not an asset
DRR and actual redemption are outside this syllabus

learn.hook: Debenture interest is the rent a company pays for borrowed money – on the face value, at the coupon rate, often twice a year.
points: Interest is calculated on the FACE (nominal) value at the coupon rate, regardless of issue price.
Many companies pay interest half-yearly: half-yearly interest = face value × rate × 6/12.

Entries: Debenture Interest A/c Dr / Debentureholders' A/c Cr (interest due); Debentureholders' A/c Dr / Bank A/c Cr (payment); Statement of Profit and Loss Dr / Debenture Interest A/c Cr (transfer at year-end).
Debenture interest is a finance cost and a charge against profit. (TDS on debenture interest is excluded from this course.)
If debentures were issued during the year, interest is only for the months they were outstanding.

example.q: A company has ₹5,00,000 10% debentures, interest payable half-yearly. Find each half-year's interest and the year's total.
steps: Year's total = ₹50,000, transferred to the Statement of Profit and Loss.

learn.reallife: PSU bonds bought by Indian pension funds pay coupons half-yearly – exactly how debenture interest is computed.

games.title: Debenture interest entries for a half-year
items: Interest becomes due: Dr Debenture Interest / Cr Debentureholders
Interest paid: Dr Debentureholders / Cr Bank
Year-end: Dr Statement of Profit and Loss / Cr Debenture Interest

quiz.q: ₹5,00,000 10% debentures; interest payable half-yearly. Interest for each half-year:
steps: Answer: ₹25,000

quiz.q: Interest on debentures is calculated on:
quiz.explain: The coupon rate applies to nominal value.
steps: The coupon rate applies to face (nominal) value.
So interest is on face value, whatever the issue price.
Answer: face value of debentures

quiz.q: 1,000 9% debentures of ₹100 were issued at ₹95. Annual interest:
quiz.explain: Interest on face value: 1,00,000 × 9%.
steps: Issue price ₹95 does not matter.
Answer: ₹9,000

quiz.q: Entry when debenture interest becomes due:
options: Debentureholders' A/c Dr / Bank A/c Cr
Statement of Profit and Loss Dr / Debenture Interest A/c Cr
Bank A/c Dr / Debenture Interest A/c Cr
Debenture Interest A/c Dr / Debentureholders' A/c Cr
quiz.explain: Interest due is an expense and a liability to holders until paid.
steps: Interest due is an expense and a liability to holders.
Entry: Debenture Interest A/c Dr, Debentureholders' A/c Cr.
Answer: Debenture Interest A/c Dr / Debentureholders' A/c Cr

quiz.q: ₹2,00,000 9% debentures were issued on 1 July; the year ends 31 March. Interest for the year:
quiz.explain: Outstanding for 9 months: 2,00,000 × 9% × 9/12.
steps: Answer: ₹13,500

quiz.q: At the year-end, debenture interest is transferred by:
options: Debenture Interest A/c Dr / Statement of Profit and Loss Cr
Statement of Profit and Loss Dr / Debenture Interest A/c Cr
Debentureholders' A/c Dr / Statement of Profit and Loss Cr
Securities Premium A/c Dr / Debenture Interest A/c Cr
quiz.explain: Interest is an expense charged to profit.
steps: At year-end, interest is charged to profit.
Entry: Statement of Profit and Loss Dr, Debenture Interest A/c Cr.
Answer: Statement of Profit and Loss Dr / Debenture Interest A/c Cr

quiz.q: In the Statement of Profit and Loss, debenture interest is shown under:
quiz.explain: Interest on borrowings is a finance cost.
steps: Interest on borrowings is shown under Finance Costs.
Answer: Finance Costs

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): Debenture interest must be paid even when the company suffers a loss.
Reason (R): Debenture interest is a charge against profits, not an appropriation.
options: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
quiz.explain: A charge must be met regardless of profit.
steps: A: debenture interest is payable even in a loss – true.
R: it is a charge, not an appropriation – true.
A charge must be met regardless of profit.
So both are true and R correctly explains A.
Answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

teach.ask: Gappu's company pays debenture interest twice a year. Explain the calculation and entries.
teach.praise: Spot on! Interest on face value, half-yearly accruals, payment, and transfer to the Statement of Profit and Loss.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: is interest worked out on the issue price or the face value?

revise.summary: Debenture interest is calculated on face value at the coupon rate (half-yearly if so payable), only for months outstanding. It is credited to Debentureholders when due, paid through bank and charged to the Statement of Profit and Loss as a finance cost.
remember: Interest = face value × rate (× months/12)
Due: Debenture Interest Dr / Debentureholders Cr
Year-end: Statement of P&L Dr / Debenture Interest Cr
Finance Costs
traps: Don't calculate interest on issue price
Interest is a charge, not an appropriation
Charge interest only for months the debentures were outstanding

topics.title: Writing off discount or loss on issue of debentures

learn.hook: A discount on issue is a cost of borrowing. Don't carry it around for years – write it off in the year of allotment.
points: Discount or loss on issue of debentures is written off in the year the debentures are allotted.
Order: first from Securities Premium (if any balance exists), then the balance from the Statement of Profit and Loss as a finance cost.
Entry: Securities Premium A/c Dr, Statement of Profit and Loss Dr / Discount (or Loss) on Issue of Debentures A/c Cr.
Using securities premium for this purpose is allowed by Section 52 of the Companies Act, 2013.

example.q: Loss on issue of debentures is ₹60,000. Securities Premium has a balance of ₹40,000. Write off the loss.
steps: Use securities premium first: ₹40,000.
Balance ₹20,000 from Statement of Profit and Loss.
Securities Premium Dr 40,000; Statement of P&L Dr 20,000 / Loss on Issue of Debentures Cr 60,000.
example.answer: ₹40,000 from premium, ₹20,000 from Statement of Profit and Loss

learn.reallife: Indian companies clean up such issue costs quickly so their balance sheets don't carry 'fictitious' items that analysts frown upon.

items.text: Discount on issue is written off in the year of ___.
It is first written off from Securities ___.
The balance is charged to the Statement of Profit and Loss as a ___ cost.

items.q: Loss ₹15,000; no premium: charged to P&L
1,000 debentures of ₹100 at ₹96, at par redemption: discount

quiz.q: Loss on issue ₹60,000; Securities Premium balance ₹40,000. Amount written off to the Statement of Profit and Loss:
quiz.explain: Premium absorbs ₹40,000 first; the remaining ₹20,000 goes to P&L.
steps: Use Securities Premium first: ₹40,000.
Rest to the Statement of Profit and Loss = 60,000 − 40,000 = ₹20,000.
Answer: ₹20,000
quiz.mistake: Charges the whole loss to profit

quiz.q: Discount or loss on issue of debentures is written off:
options: over the life of the debentures always
in the year of allotment of debentures
never; it stays as an asset
quiz.explain: The current approach is to write it off in the year of allotment.
steps: Under the current approach, discount or loss is written off in the year of allotment.
Answer: in the year of allotment of debentures
quiz.mistake: Spreads it over the debenture life

quiz.q: The first source used to write off discount on issue of debentures is:
quiz.explain: Section 52 allows premium to absorb it; the rest goes to P&L.
steps: Section 52 allows Securities Premium to absorb discount on debentures.
So it is the first source used.
Answer: Securities Premium

quiz.q: Discount on issue ₹30,000; Securities Premium ₹50,000. Securities Premium remaining after write-off:
quiz.explain: ₹30,000 is used from premium, leaving ₹20,000.
steps: Discount ₹30,000 is fully absorbed by premium.
Remaining premium = 50,000 − 30,000 = ₹20,000.
Answer: ₹20,000

quiz.q: Entry to write off ₹60,000 loss using ₹40,000 premium and the rest from profit:
options: Securities Premium Dr 40,000; Statement of P&L Dr 20,000 / Loss on Issue of Debentures Cr 60,000
Loss on Issue Dr 60,000 / Securities Premium Cr 40,000, Statement of P&L Cr 20,000
Statement of P&L Dr 60,000 / Securities Premium Cr 60,000
Securities Premium Dr 60,000 / Loss on Issue Cr 60,000
quiz.explain: Both sources are debited and the loss account is closed.
steps: Debit both sources and close the loss account.
Entry: Securities Premium Dr 40,000; Statement of P&L Dr 20,000 / Loss on Issue Cr 60,000.
Answer: Securities Premium Dr 40,000; Statement of P&L Dr 20,000 / Loss on Issue of Debentures Cr 60,000

quiz.q: When charged to the Statement of Profit and Loss, the discount on issue of debentures is shown as:
quiz.explain: It is a cost of borrowing.
steps: Discount on issue of debentures is a cost of borrowing.
So it is shown as a finance cost.
Answer: finance cost

quiz.q: 1,000 debentures of ₹100 issued at ₹96, redeemable at par; no securities premium exists. Amount charged to profit in the year of allotment:
quiz.explain: Discount ₹4 × 1,000, fully charged as there is no premium.
steps: Discount = 100 − 96 = ₹4 per debenture; no premium exists.
Charged to profit = 1,000 × 4 = ₹4,000.
Answer: ₹4,000

quiz.q:
Assertion (A): Securities premium can be used to write off loss on issue of debentures.
Reason (R): Securities premium can be distributed as cash dividend.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is false, but R is true
A is true, but R is false
quiz.explain: A is true under Section 52, but premium can never be used for dividend, so R is false.
steps: A: securities premium can write off loss on issue – true (Section 52).
R: premium can be paid as dividend – false.
So A is true, but R is false.
Answer: A is true, but R is false
quiz.mistake: Thinks premium is a free reserve

teach.ask: Gappu has a discount on debentures in his books. Explain how and when to write it off.
teach.praise: Perfect! Write it off in the year of allotment – first from securities premium, then from profit as finance cost.
teach.nudge: Gappu asks: what if there's not enough securities premium?

revise.summary: Discount or loss on issue of debentures is written off in the year of allotment, first from Securities Premium (Section 52) and the balance from the Statement of Profit and Loss as a finance cost.
focus: Order of writing off discount or loss
remember: Write off in the year of allotment
First Securities Premium, then Statement of P&L
Entry: Securities Premium Dr, Statement of P&L Dr / Discount (or Loss) on Issue Cr
traps: Securities premium cannot be paid as dividend
Use securities premium before charging profit
Don't spread the write-off over the debentures' life under this method
